items.stem: What is abstraction?
options: Removing unnecessary details to focus on the essential features of a problem
Writing code in a high-level language
Breaking a problem into smaller parts
items.answer: Removing unnecessary details to focus on the essential features of a problem
items.markingKey: Abstraction keeps only what is relevant (e.g. a metro map shows stations and lines, not distances).

items.stem: Explain two benefits of decomposition when developing a large program.
items.answer: Each sub-problem is easier to understand and solve; modules can be written and tested by different programmers at the same time; modules can be reused.

items.stem: Explain why abstraction is useful when designing a computer model of a real system.
items.answer: It removes irrelevant details so the model is simpler, faster to build and run, and focuses on the factors that affect the result.

items.stem: Jonas is designing a mobile game in which a player moves through a city collecting coins. Explain how decomposition helps a team of programmers work on this project.
items.answer: Sub-problems assigned to different programmers, developed and tested in parallel, then combined.

items.stem: A school wants a program to produce student timetables. (a) Explain how decomposition helps a team of programmers work on this project. (b) Explain how one module from this project could be reused in another project.
items.answer: (a) Sub-problems assigned to different programmers, developed and tested in parallel, then combined. (b) e.g. a validation or login module can be used unchanged in a different program, saving time.

items.stem: Palm Grove Hotel in Cairo is building a route-planning app for its delivery drivers. (a) Use abstraction to describe the data the system needs to store and what can be ignored. (b) Explain how pattern recognition could save development time.
items.answer: (a) Keep only the data needed for processing (e.g. locations, connections and times; or books, members and loans); ignore appearance and unrelated details. (b) Identifying that tasks (e.g. searching lists) are similar means one routine can be written and reused.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is decomposition?

items.answer: Breaking a complex problem down into smaller, more manageable sub-problems
items.markingKey: Each sub-problem can be solved (and coded as a module) separately.

items.stem: Which is an example of abstraction?

items.answer: A train map that shows stations and connections but not exact distances

items.stem: Horizon Travel in Karachi is planning a new computer system. Explain how decomposition would help the team.

items.stem: What is an algorithm?
options: A program written in machine code
A sequence of steps that can be carried out to perform a task
items.answer: A sequence of steps that can be carried out to perform a task
items.markingKey: Algorithms can be shown in structured English, flowcharts or pseudocode.

items.stem: Explain why pseudocode is used to design algorithms.
items.answer: It is independent of any programming language so it can be understood by all programmers and easily converted to code; it focuses on logic, not syntax.

items.stem: Explain why meaningful identifier names should be used.
items.answer: They make the algorithm/code easier to read, understand, debug and maintain, by the author and by others.

items.stem: Omar needs an algorithm for Northfield Academy to input 25 marks and output their average. Write the algorithm in pseudocode, declaring all variables.
items.answer:
DECLARE Total : REAL
DECLARE Value : INTEGER
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
Total ← 0
FOR Count ← 1 TO 25
    INPUT Value
    Total ← Total + Value
NEXT Count
OUTPUT Total / 25
items.markingKey: Mark points: initialise total; loop 25 times; input inside loop; add to total; output total / 25. 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: What is stepwise refinement?
options: Converting a flowchart into a structure chart
Testing an algorithm with many inputs
Breaking each step of an algorithm into smaller, more detailed steps until each can be coded directly
Removing unnecessary steps from an algorithm
items.answer: Breaking each step of an algorithm into smaller, more detailed steps until each can be coded directly
items.markingKey: Top-down design: refine until each step is a single instruction or simple module.

items.stem: Explain the benefits of stepwise refinement.
items.answer: Each step becomes simple to understand and code; errors are easier to find; the steps can become modules shared among a team.

items.stem: Omar is using stepwise refinement to design a program for Horizon Travel. Explain why refinement can stop at different depths for different steps.
items.answer: Some steps are simple and can be coded at once; others need several levels.

items.stem: A team at Nova Telecom is refining an algorithm before coding it. Explain how stepwise refinement helps the team to share the work.

items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: In Cambridge pseudocode, which symbol is used for assignment?

This algorithm should input 6 prices and output the average.
Total ← 0
FOR Count ← 1 TO 6
    INPUT Value
    Total ← Total + Value
    OUTPUT Total / 6
NEXT Count
Identify the error and explain how to correct it.
items.answer: The OUTPUT is inside the loop so a value is output every time; it should be moved after NEXT Count.

items.stem:
This algorithm should input 5 scores and output the average.
Total ← 0
FOR Count ← 1 TO 4
    INPUT Value
    Total ← Total + Value
NEXT Count
OUTPUT Total / 5
Identify the error and explain how to correct it.
items.answer: The loop runs only 4 times; line 2 should be FOR Count ← 1 TO 5.

items.stem:
Study the pseudocode algorithm.
X ← 3
Turns ← 0
WHILE X < 54
    X ← X * 3
    Turns ← Turns + 1
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT X, " ", Turns
State the output.
items.markingKey: X takes the values 3, 9, 27, 81; loop runs 3 times [2]

items.stem: Grace is writing a program for SwiftCar Rentals. Complete an identifier table giving a suitable identifier and data type for each of: a customer's surname; the average temperature; a counter for the loop.
items.answer: Surname : STRING; AverageTemp : REAL; Count : INTEGER
items.markingKey: 1 mark per row with meaningful identifier and correct data type: a customer's surname → Surname STRING; the average temperature → AverageTemp REAL; a counter for the loop → Count INTEGER [3]

items.stem: Priya needs an algorithm for Coral Bay Aquarium to input 21 ages and output how many are greater than 76. Write the algorithm in pseudocode, declaring all variables.
items.answer:
DECLARE Value : INTEGER
DECLARE Count, Above : INTEGER
Above ← 0
FOR Count ← 1 TO 21
    INPUT Value
    IF Value > 76 THEN
        Above ← Above + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT Count
OUTPUT Above
items.markingKey: Mark points: initialise counter to 0; loop 21 times; input in loop; IF value > 76; increment counter and output after loop. 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem:
An algorithm is shown in pseudocode.
X ← 5
Count ← 0
WHILE X < 165
    X ← X * 2
    Count ← Count + 1
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT X, " ", Count
(a) State the output. (b) Identify the type of loop used and explain why it is suitable. (c) Describe how the algorithm would be shown as a flowchart, naming the symbols used.
items.answer: (a) 320 6 (b) pre-condition WHILE loop: may run zero times, condition checked first (c) terminators for start/stop, rectangles for assignments, diamond for the loop condition with Yes/No branches, parallelogram for output, arrows showing the loop back
items.markingKey: (a) X takes the values 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320; loop runs 6 times [2] (b) loop type [1]; reason [1] (c) correct symbols [2]

items.stem:
An algorithm is shown in pseudocode.
Number ← 170
Count ← 0
REPEAT
    Number ← Number DIV 2
    Count ← Count + 1
UNTIL Number = 0
OUTPUT Count
(a) State the output. (b) Identify the type of loop used and explain why it is suitable. (c) Describe how the algorithm would be shown as a flowchart, naming the symbols used.
items.answer: (a) 8 (b) post-condition REPEAT loop: runs at least once (c) terminators for start/stop, rectangles for assignments, diamond for the loop condition with Yes/No branches, parallelogram for output, arrows showing the loop back
items.markingKey: (a) Number becomes 85, 42, 21, 10, 5, 2, 1, 0; Count = 8 [2] (b) loop type [1]; reason [1] (c) correct symbols [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) When should stepwise refinement stop? (b) What is stepwise refinement?
items.answer: (a) When each step is detailed enough to be written directly as program code (b) Breaking each step of an algorithm into smaller, more detailed steps until each can be coded directly
items.markingKey: (a) Each final step corresponds to one or a few statements. (b) Top-down design: refine until each step is a single instruction or simple module.

items.stem: Daniel is using stepwise refinement to design a program for BlueWave Supermarkets. Explain why the top-level steps are not detailed enough to code.
items.answer: Each top-level step represents a large task needing many statements; it must be broken down further.

items.stem: Mei is using stepwise refinement to design a program for Lakeside College. (a) Explain why the top-level steps are not detailed enough to code. (b) Explain how stepwise refinement makes testing easier.
items.answer: (a) Each top-level step represents a large task needing many statements; it must be broken down further. (b) Each small step/module can be tested separately before being combined, so errors are easier to locate.

items.stem: A team at Orbit Games Studio is refining an algorithm before coding it. Explain how stepwise refinement helps the team to share the work.
items.answer: Each refined step can become a module written and tested by a different person.

items.stem: Mateo is designing a program for SkyLink Airways in Seoul. (a) Explain how you know when refinement is complete. (b) Explain how stepwise refinement helps the team to share the work.
items.answer: (a) Each step can be translated directly into one or a few program statements. (b) Each refined step can become a module written and tested by a different person.

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Auckland needs a program to "process a customer order". (a) Use stepwise refinement to give the top-level steps. (b) Refine the step "Calculate the total cost" further. (c) Write pseudocode for one of your refined steps. (d) Explain one advantage of designing the solution in this way.
items.answer: (a) Input order details; Validate the order; Calculate the total cost; Update stock levels; Output a receipt (b) Set Total to 0; For each item, multiply quantity by price and add to Total; If Total > 100, apply 10% discount; Add delivery charge (c) e.g. pseudocode for add delivery charge (d) easier to code/test each step; modules can be shared
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per sensible step, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark per refined step, max 3 [3] (c) correct pseudocode syntax and logic [2] (d) [1]
